status_summary: Executive Order 14148 (signed 2025-01-20) revoked Executive Order 14094 (Modernizing Regulatory Review, 2023), and Executive Order 14192 (signed 2025-01-31) directed the OMB Director to revoke the 2023 Circular A-4 and reinstate the 2003 version, which is the only version on OMB's circulars page; EO 14192 also requires agencies to identify at least 10 existing regulations for repeal for each new one and lets the OMB Director set agency cost allowances, and a Columbia Law School climate blog treats it as the successor to Executive Order 13771, which it does not name. Executive Order 14294 (signed 2025-05-09) disfavors criminal enforcement of regulatory offenses and requires agencies to report such offenses and state mental-state standards in new rules, covering the subject of first-term Executive Order 13980 without naming or reinstating it. The 2026 Unified Agenda introduction (2026-08-14) reports $211.8 billion in cost savings for fiscal 2025 and projects $1.5 trillion for fiscal 2026 (administration figures), and a Wikipedia list counts 22 Congressional Review Act disapproval resolutions signed in 2025. No enacted REINS Act or Midnight Rules Relief Act, administrative pay-as-you-go requirement, updated federalism or takings order, or confirmed revival of Executive Order 13891 or the other listed first-term orders was found.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14148 revokes Executive Order 14094 (Modernizing Regulatory Review, 2023), along with Executive Orders 13992, 13990 and 14008. It does not mention Circular A-4.

Executive Order 14192 (published 2025-02-06) requires agencies to identify at least 10 existing regulations for repeal for each new one, sets a fiscal 2025 total incremental cost for new regulations below zero, lets the OMB Director set later cost allowances, directs revocation of the 2023 Circular A-4 and reinstatement of the 2003 version, and reinstates the 2018 Treasury and OMB agreement on tax-regulation review.

Executive Order 14294, Fighting Overcriminalization in Federal Regulations, is signed (published 2025-05-14, 90 FR 20363). It disfavors criminal enforcement of regulatory offenses, requires agencies to report their criminal regulatory offenses to OMB and post them, to state a mental-state standard in new rules with criminal consequences, and to publish guidance on referrals to the Justice Department. It covers the subject of first-term Executive Order 13980 but does not name or revoke any prior order.

Congressional Review Act disapproval resolutions on BLM resource management plans are signed, the latest of 22 such resolutions a Wikipedia list counts as signed in 2025 (others include three California vehicle waiver resolutions on 2025-06-12 and two CFPB rule resolutions on 2025-05-09).

The 2026 Unified Agenda introduction describes Executive Order 14192's ten-for-one rule and agency designations as deregulatory, regulatory, exempt, waived or other, and reports $211.8 billion in cost savings for fiscal 2025 and a projected $1.5 trillion for fiscal 2026.
